Command: Do Not Eat Flesh with Its Blood
Summary: The Noahic food prohibition: flesh with its lifeblood still in it must not be eaten.
Commandment: Do not eat flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof.
Application: Given to Noah and his sons as part of the post-flood order, before Sinai and before any Jewish identity existed. Debated: some hold this Noahic prohibition still binds all humanity and note the Jerusalem council's abstain-from-blood instruction (Acts 15:29); others hold it belonged to the pre-Mosaic order and passed with the old covenant's food laws. The site does not settle this.
Purpose: To honor life as residing in the blood; Genesis 9:4 states the prohibition without a stated expiry, which is why its duration is debated rather than settled here.
Function: Life resides in the blood, and this Noahic prohibition honours that. This command predates Sinai — it was given to Noah and his sons before any Jewish identity existed — so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it; whether it still binds all humanity is debated, and this entry does not settle it. Its goal was to honour life as residing in the blood. The evil it addressed was eating flesh with its lifeblood still in it, treating life cheaply. It restrained that evil by the prohibition itself, given without a stated expiry in Genesis 9:4.
